P1.evidence: Setter notes were referenced but deliberately not read back — 'So he just briefed me in on your situation. Yes. But I'm kind of old-school, and I like to hear it from the person directly.' The frame was three-part: 'what's been going on, like what you're striving towards too... And how can we actually help you and support you? And if we can, I will show you exactly how Trevor works.' No 'what's in the way' and no 'what you need'. Frame agreement was asked and got a strong yes — 'Cool? Okay, good' / 'I'm glad to hear that, because I'm personally, myself, very old-school as well.' Open question ran: 'in your own words, like what's the main thing that you're trying to fix or make it better right now?'

P2.evidence: The baseline phase was effectively skipped. Height and weight were never asked and are not in the transcript. Age surfaced only because the rep volunteered his own ('It's funny. I'm 55'). Occupation was never asked — the rep learned he works in fashion at 01:03:22, an hour in, and only because the prospect used it to argue about pricing. No health conditions question. No injuries, chronic pain or movement-limitation question at any point, for a 55-year-old about to be sold loaded ballistic kettlebell work. No sleep question. No energy question. Training week was only partially covered via the gym membership and the unused kettlebells. Diet was the one clean hit: 'the nutrition part because you're a vegan, right?... I imagine you eat clean, yeah?... Any vices, any, you know, sweet tooth?'

P3.evidence: The why-bridge and the reflect-back are the two best moves on the call. P3d ran repeatedly and patiently — 'what's your why? What's your why behind that, why you want to do it?' and 'where does those, this urge comes from?' — and produced real material: 'partly frustration, partly disappointment... it's all about discipline, and I haven't had the discipline.' P3h landed cleanly: 'it's not about the aesthetics... it's more about who you become and how you're going to feel when you're going to accomplish the goal... Is that correct?' answered 'Yes. Yes.' But the specific goal questions never ran — no 'what would you change, one thing', no mobility/strength/energy question, no 'something physical you want to do but can't'. P3f was actively refused by the prospect ('It's not something that has anything to do with my environment') and the rep answered with a generic monologue about parents and husbands rather than testing it on him.

P4.evidence: Strongest phase. 'Those kettlebells have been sitting since COVID in your garage, in your garden. So what kept you, what stopped you from actually putting it into work?' is exactly the move, and he stayed on it through two deflections — when the prospect said motivation, the rep pushed back ('motivation is just an emotion. It comes and goes'), and when the prospect said the timing wasn't right, he pushed again ('What makes it right? What makes it right time right now?'). The prospect named the gap himself: 'for me, what works always the best is to have a plan, a plan, or a program, or routine.' P4f is only partial — the motivation-is-an-emotion reframe is adjacent to 'the information isn't the problem' but the actual question was never put.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame ran before the offer. He was never asked what the next two years look like if nothing changes, never asked whether he was willing to settle for it, never asked why not, and never asked to draw a line in the sand. The deathbed frame at 01:05:33 — 'when you're going to be on your deathbed in 40 years... are you going to be thinking about those 6, 4K?' — is an objection rebuttal about money, not a cost-of-inaction frame, and it arrived fifty minutes after the price. Against a prospect who is fit, happy and states 'For my age, I'm in a good shape', the absence of a consequence frame left the whole call resting on wanting a programme, which is worth far less than $6,000 to him.

P6.evidence: P6b ran explicitly: 'If we can figure out the rest of the details. Are you fully committed to actually doing this, showing up and...' The answer was a clear not-yet — 'at this point, not yet because I haven't made the commitment' — and later 'I don't know enough yet, like, how it breaks down.' Under P6c that is the trigger to return to Phase 5. The rep instead walked him through the investment nine minutes later. Belief in the method was never checked with the scripted question; the prospect volunteered it unprompted ('I believe in the program... I don't have a doubt'), which under the scoring rule is not credit for asking.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted at three price points and refused at all three, so payment, the Trevor onboarding booking, the agreement signature and the welcome-email steps were never reachable.

objection_plays.detail: The isolate ran twice and ran well — 'it is more importantly for me is how do you feel with the program? And if you would like to commit to it, and then we can talk about finances', and later 'the price is the only thing that is stopping you.' The rep also correctly diagnosed the objection type live: 'it's not even the price stopping you because you have the money, you could do it, you could do it even probably upfront, but it's the justification of actually spending on that amount of money on yourself.' After that, nothing scripted ran. No SHOULD-versus-HOW frame. No 'most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up'. No permission question about an open, honest financial conversation. Zero of the six financial-picture questions: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no credit card count, no available credit, no used-versus-available, no investments. The play was replaced by a financing link and then by a new price.

'Maybe in a year's time, I'm willing to spend 6K in this... But at this point, no' is squarely OD. The rep started the play properly — 'But what's going to be the difference in your time from now?', 'And in a year's time, it's not going to be too much?', 'Come on, let's be serious. What will change in your mindset in one year in terms of...' — which is the 'when does it actually become the right time' move. He then abandoned it when the prospect deflected with a joke about starting a competing programme, and never came back. None of the compounding-cost moves ran (metabolism, injuries, the only thing you can control is right now).

'This takes some serious thinking' landed at 01:00:21 and the rep answered it by sending a financing link. None of the play ran — no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', no 'what makes you feel it can', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now'. Ironically the prospect had already volunteered the answer to the first move ('I believe in the program... I don't have a doubt'), which is the strongest possible setup for OA, and it was not used.

New script gap, not covered by the two already logged. This is a value objection from a prospect with confirmed capacity: 'I can pay the 6K. That we know. But I don't think this thing is worth it with Trevor, with anyone else either.' Objection C is built for a wallet that is closed; here the wallet is open and the buyer has run his own margin analysis — he develops product for a fashion brand and explicitly reasons from cost to make, using a EUR 16,000 Miu Miu jacket as the analogy for what he thinks Primal is doing. There is no scripted move for a professional price-auditor. The rep improvised down-market (a $4,000 tier, then a $1,200 trial), which is the worst available response to someone whose objection is that the price signals overcharging — every reduction confirmed his thesis.

Second script gap: brand and cultural mismatch. 'It's very American, it's super American... I keep getting these messages, it actually turns me totally off... is this, again, another automated?' and at the close 'I think it's good, but I don't think we match.' There is no scripted play for a prospect who trusts the coach but is repelled by the marketing wrapper around him. The rep confirmed the messaging is AI and defended it operationally, which conceded the point. This objection was never resolved and reappeared as the final reason given.

notes: Phase 4 was genuinely excellent and Phase 2 barely happened — no height, weight, occupation, health, injury, sleep or energy questions at all. The call then went from a hedged 'at this point, not yet' straight to price with no consequence frame, so an eighty-minute conversation reached the number with no cost of inaction attached to it. Once the objection landed the rep correctly identified it as value rather than affordability and then treated it as affordability anyway, cutting price three times against a buyer who had already told him the price was the signal he distrusted. Coach: run P2 before anything else, and when the wallet is confirmed open, stop discounting.
